correctness.rationale: The first 2h letters of a nonunary h-periodic run contain exactly two copies of one marker: zero markers would make the run unary by periodicity, and four exceed the weight. Thus the period is one of the adjacent distances, and a three-marker run requires equal gaps. A fixed pair and period determine at most one maximal interval. Equal gaps or a unit gap have exponent sums strictly below the candidate for n>=13. For distinct gaps 2<=p<q, the potential run intervals are contained in [max(0,x-p+1),x+2p) and [x+1,min(n,x+p+2q)); the upper bounds are positive even when the corresponding run is absent. Ignoring endpoint losses yields the first bound in (1); charging combined loss at least (2p+2q-1-n)_+/q yields the second. For p<=m the first bound is optimized by q=p+1 and then p=m. For p>=m+1, the second decreases with p after setting q=p+1; n<=4m+4 and m>=3 give the stated comparison. The witness contributes n-3 from the four zero runs plus the stated maximal intervals [0,3m-1) and [m,4m+1), with least periods m and m+1. At n=12 the same bounds give at most 83/6 for p<=2 and at most 9+g(3)=167/12 for p>=3; the equal/unit-gap cases are below 167/12. Markers (2,5,9) attain 9+8/3+9/4. A separate longest-border maximality enumerator checks 2,380 weight-three words at lengths 3..16, confirming the n=12 exception and the n=13..16 formula and witness. This finite replay is supplementary to the analytic proof.
residual_risks: Neither a complete equality classification nor a statement for other compositions or cyclic words is established.

value.rationale: The sum of run exponents is a standard invariant distinct from run count. Weight three is the first sparse composition permitting two unequal nonunary periods. Balancing both periods and boundary losses yields a sharp length-dependent correction, a verified sharp onset, and a uniform attaining family. This is a concrete benchmark unavailable from unrestricted bounds or the known count distribution.
residual_risks: No sharper unlimited-composition bound or entire fixed-weight exponent distribution is asserted.
